subject: MAP: Latency & Throughput acceptance criteria — hosted comparison
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@peregrinelabs.ai>, Priya Sen <priya@peregrinelabs.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Latency & Throughput acceptance criteria — hosted comparison

Thanks again for carving out time today — good discussion. High-level recap and immediate next steps so we have the MAP recorded. Attaching a first-draft MAP and a short SLO probe matrix (MAP_v1.xlsx; slo_probe_matrix.csv).

Call recap (agreements):
- Target acceptance window: p95 and p99 end-to-end (client → Redwood hosted API → model → client) across your production traffic profile.
- Peregrine current baseline (as shared on-call): p95 ~ 380ms, p99 ~ 810ms (incumbent).
- Peregrine target for go/no-go: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms for the principal user flows. We discussed that this is aggressive relative to their incumbent but feasible with streaming + small-batch tuning.
- Throughput/scale: sustained 120–150 requests/s with 10–12 concurrent streaming sessions for the primary 1–2 minute workflows.
- Behavior expectations: partial streaming chunks must arrive within ~80–120ms of token emission for the interactive flow; fallback to non-streaming retrieval for batch jobs is acceptable.

Immediate actions we committed to:
1) Redwood (Camila, Grace) will run a synthetic run using Peregrine's test harness (they provide token and test endpoint) to produce a 30-minute sustained traffic trace. Deliverable: latency histogram + p95/p99 samples (hosted_vs_incumbent_latency_samples.log). ETA: Wed 2028-05-23.
2) Peregrine (Evan) will share a reduced test dataset and a short list of 6 representative prompts (incl. expected token counts) and any IP/ACL constraints. ETA: Tue 2028-05-21.
3) Redwood (Ben) to propose the canary & traffic-shaping MOP (slicing by region and model variant) and confirm rollback thresholds. ETA: Thu 2028-05-24.
4) Joint acceptance criteria will be codified in the MAP: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms, sustained throughput for 30 minutes at 140 req/s, and streaming concurrency of 10 with <150ms median chunk latency.

Ask from you: please confirm the test-slot window (we suggested Wed 05/23 10:00-13:00 PDT), share any blackout windows, and send over the test harness key.

Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP draft), slo_probe_matrix.csv (test vectors and traffic envelope).

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0192

From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@peregrinelabs.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sen <priya@peregrinelabs.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Latency & Throughput acceptance criteria — hosted comparison

Thanks Tessa — appreciate the clear summary. Quick clarifications from our side before the run: 

- Test harness: we'll share a short-lived API key (DEV_KEY_ple_2028) and a reduced dataset (6 prompts + 20 synthetic permutations) by EOD today. The harness will simulate token emission patterns that match our interactive clients (avg 55 tokens, 90th percentile 160 tokens).
- Streaming semantics: when you say "chunk latency" we mean time from model token generation to first chunk arriving to client. Our current provider often batches aggressively for cost reasons; we need to ensure Redwood preserves low-latency emission even with batching.
- Incumbent baseline: the numbers I quoted are for our primary region (us-west). We can send a short log excerpt (anonymized) if it helps.

Also — small ask on instrumentation: please include server-side traces with request IDs in the returned headers so our telemetry can stitch traces end-to-end.

Happy to take the Wed 10:00–13:00 PDT slot if you can confirm.

On Wed we plan to run a lightweight functional pass first, then the 30-minute sustained throughput run.

—Evan
Peregrine Labs

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: FW: MAP: Latency & Throughput acceptance criteria — hosted comparison

Looping in engineering details and owners. Notes for the run prep: 

- Camila: own the synthetic-run orchestration — ensure we run with both streaming enabled and streaming disabled (to compare tail behavior). Use the slo_probe_matrix.csv vectors that Tessa attached.
- Grace: instrument KV cache warmups and confirm model-variant switching is exercised. We need per-request headers for request_id, bucket, and model_variant. Add brief note in the run doc about kernel selection (int8 quantized path vs fp16) so ops knows which image to use.
- Tessa: I'll draft the rollback thresholds (simple: if p99 degrades >20% vs baseline or error rate >0.8% within 5 minutes, rollback).

I'll attach the latency sample file after the run for the external colleague to review.

Thanks — Ben
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: MAP: Latency & Throughput acceptance criteria — hosted comparison

Thanks — confirmed for Wed 05/23 10:00–13:00 PDT (we will start with a 15-minute functional pass at 10:00, then begin the sustained 30-minute throughput window at 10:30).

Test key (temporary): DEV_KEY_ple_2028 (expires 2028-05-25 23:59 PDT). Endpoint: https://test-api.redwood.com/v1/ple-probe.

Acceptance criteria (finalized for MAP):
- p95 end-to-end <= 250ms
- p99 end-to-end <= 450ms
- Sustained throughput: 140 req/s for 30 continuous minutes (95% of the window)
- Streaming concurrency: 10 concurrent interactive sessions with median chunk latency < 150ms
- Error budget: total request error rate <= 0.5% during acceptance window

MOP summary (high-level):
1) Functional smoke (10:00–10:15): validate auth, model selection, streaming enablement, header injection.
2) Warmup (10:15–10:30): KV cache warmups and short bursts up to 40 req/s.
3) Sustained run (10:30–11:00): 140 req/s, monitor p95/p99, error rate, and chunk latencies.
4) Shadow run (optional): if sustained run passes, we will run a 30-minute shadow against a small percentage of live traffic next week.

Deliverables from Redwood after run: latency histograms, per-request samples (hosted_vs_incumbent_latency_samples.log), raw traces with request_id headers, and a short go/no-go recommendation note.

See HubSpot deal for the MAP & timeline: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/3497

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
